statusText: Mapped policy state: STRONG_BLOCK_NO_NEW_RISK. The freshest verified Micro-NQ evidence remains strongly downside-efficient, while no newer reliable live NQ path was available at the assessment cutoff.
recommendation: High Tail reflects the latest verified downside structure. De-escalation would require observed two-way rotation, deeper retracements or a sustained reclaim; continued shallow rebounds or fresh lows would keep the state restrictive.
headline: Downside efficiency remains strong; lack of newer verified live structure caps further escalation.
body: At 08:47 UTC delayed Micro-NQ remained Strong Sell with RSI 21.7, ADX 71.1, MACD -90.7 and negative Highs/Lows. The U.S. 10-year was near 5.116% and Brent near $102.18; Cboe VIX futures were near 17.75. Shared Finviz context was stale beyond 90 minutes and excluded.

sources.title: September 24 market brief: yields, oil and futures

lookbackSummary: Tail rose through the September 23 selloff, eased as mean reversion returned overnight, then rebuilt from low/watch levels to Tail 37 by the 09:00 UTC September 24 assessment. Prior hourly opinions are preserved from published history.
outlookSummary: Current high Tail is anchored to the latest verified downside-efficiency evidence rather than event importance alone. The concentrated 12:20-15:15 UTC catalyst window raises Stress; future high Tail requires observed weak retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding.

forecast.analysis: Freshest verified Micro-NQ evidence remains the 08:47 UTC Strong Sell snapshot: RSI 21.7, ADX 71.1, MACD -90.7 and negative Highs/Lows. No newer reliable live NQ path was verified by the cutoff, so high Tail is retained but not escalated.
drivers: 08:47 UTC Strong Sell remains freshest verified NQ evidence

forecast.analysis: Elevated Tail into the next hour requires the earlier downside impulse to keep producing shallow rebounds or fresh lows. A sustained reclaim and broader two-way rotation would weaken the one-way-path case.

Claims and BEA international data are due at 12:30 UTC, followed by Hammack at 12:50. Stress is extreme; high Tail requires the observed post-release path to extend directionally with weak retracements.
drivers: Initial claims and BEA data at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: Into the 13:30 UTC cash open, high Tail is conditional on post-data pressure carrying into the opening auction with repeated extension, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.
New-home sales is scheduled for 14:00 UTC. The modeled peak requires actual opening/data continuation with shallow pullbacks or failed retracements; no release result or reaction is assumed.

High Tail after the opening sequence persists only if directional progress continues without meaningful mean reversion. Broad rotation, deeper pullbacks or a sustained reclaim would support de-escalation.
By 16:00 UTC, elevated Tail remains conditional on the opening trend surviving. Two-way trade, wider rotations and volatility decay would reduce the probability of a prolonged mean-reversion failure.
Late-morning Tail stays elevated only if earlier directional pressure remains unresolved. A balanced range or repeated full retracements would argue for further de-escalation.
Tail sits at the elevated threshold conditionally. Session-extreme holding or another failed retracement would sustain it; broader rotations would not.
Early-afternoon Tail moves to WATCH unless a fresh directional leg emerges. The base case assumes some retracement capacity returns after the morning catalyst cluster.
Later-afternoon WATCH assumes rotations persist and directional efficiency fades. A renewed one-way break would invalidate the de-escalating path.
Later-session WATCH assumes no fresh persistent extension and some normalization in pullback depth. Near-extreme holding would keep risk from de-escalating.
Late-session Tail falls to low only if price discovery is two-sided. A renewed extension into the close would invalidate this path.
Post-close Tail remains low if the U.S. session ends without a renewed no-retracement move. Cross-asset Stress can remain high even while Tail de-escalates.
drivers: Cross-asset Stress remains separate from Tail

forecast.analysis: Overnight Tail is low if the prior move stabilizes and meaningful retracements remain available. No Asia-session direction is assumed in advance.
Tail remains low if no geopolitical discontinuity or renewed rates shock creates fresh directional efficiency. Any such break would require reassessment.
Quiet-hour Tail stays low while price remains rotational and repeated extension is absent. Elevated macro Stress can persist separately.
Pre-Europe Tail stays low if structure remains two-sided. A new lower-low sequence with shallow rebounds would invalidate the low-Tail path.
As Europe approaches, low Tail depends on a rotational liquidity transition rather than a clean directional break. Cross-asset alignment remains a checkpoint.
Europe-open Tail moves to WATCH conditionally because repricing can restore trend efficiency. No fresh one-way path is assumed before it is observed.
European-morning WATCH assumes cross-asset pressure but still-available NQ retracements. Repeated extension would require escalation.
Later European-morning WATCH reflects Friday event proximity raising Stress while Tail remains tied to observed price-path behavior.
Tail reaches upper WATCH ahead of Friday's Williams and durable-goods checkpoints, conditional on no renewed persistent trend before those events.
At 09:00 UTC Friday, Tail remains WATCH ahead of Williams at 09:15 UTC. Event proximity raises Stress; Tail stays below blocking unless one-way price behavior is actually observed.
drivers: Event proximity raises Stress, not Tail by itself
